steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Observational drawing means working from direct looking — not imagination or photographs (unless for specific purpose).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Sight-size measuring helps you judge proportions accurately by comparing sizes at arm's length with a pencil or thread.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Linear perspective creates the illusion of depth: one-point for front-facing views, two-point for corners, aerial for distance.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Foreshortening describes how objects appear shorter when angled towards or away from the viewer.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring observational and analytical drawing. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with observational and analytical drawing. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with observational and analytical drawing. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to observational and analytical drawing, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to ref | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
